Dataset scope, attribution & learning references

BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science licensed under CC Attribution 4.0 International. Database description · Dataset licence · CC BY 4.0.

All 2,234 unique source mesh IDs from BodyParts3D 4.0 are retained. Optimised mesh files and English names are sourced from Human Atlas, whose adaptations include coordinate conversion, mesh simplification and compressed binary packing. This lesson adds display filters, per-part visibility and separation, recolouring, search and anatomy practice. Geometry is not registered to the separate heart reference model.

These are 2,234 modelled parts, not a claim that the human body has only 2,234 anatomical structures. Some names repeat for separately modelled segments; IDs distinguish them. The 15 display groups are navigation categories, not a claim of 15 standard organ systems. Coverage is uneven: for example, the lymphatic group contains the spleen and thymic lobes, not a complete lymphatic network. The dataset depicts one adult male reference and does not represent every variation.

Original introductory group summaries, cross-checked against OpenStax’s body organisation overview. Source labels remain English. Hausa summaries await educator review. Educational study aid; not a clinical or surgical guide. Three.js and fflate are used under MIT licences.
